podcast.body: Originally titled "Hitchhiker," Kurt Cobain wrote the first version of this song in June 1987 after reading a newspaper story about a 14-year-old girl who was kidnapped, raped, and tortured by Gerald Frant but managed to escape. The song was first recorded during the "Blue EP" sessions in 1989, refined during the "Nevermind" sessions, and the album version is a remix of that demo. During a 1991 *Nevermind* tour performance of "Polly," two individuals in the audience sexually assaulted a girl, leading Kurt Cobain to refer to them as "two wastes of sperm and eggs" in the *Incesticide* album liner notes. "Paulie based on a true story of kidnapping, rape and torture."

podcast.body: This song was inspired by a June 1987 newspaper story Kurt Cobain read about a 14-year-old girl, referred to as Paulie, who was kidnapped at gunpoint by serial rapist Gerald Frant. Frant, who had previously served time for raping a 12-year-old, abducted Paulie after she hitchhiked home from a concert at the Community World Theatre in Tacoma, Washington. She was taken to Frant's trailer and tortured with whips, razors, and a blowtorch while tied to a pulley apparatus, but managed to escape from his van during a stop for gas. Frant was arrested the next day and is serving two consecutive 75-year sentences. The song was initially titled "Hitchhiker" and first recorded during the Blue EP sessions, then refined during the Nevermind sessions, with the album version being a remixed demo. During a 1991 Nevermind tour performance of "Polly," two audience members sexually assaulted a girl, an incident Kurt Cobain condemned in the liner notes of the Incestosite album. "Kurt was really moved by this story and wrote the first version of a song that he called Hitchhiker when Nirvana was getting ready to record the Bleach album in 1989."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
